data.cheatsheetTitle: Kernel-checked Stable AC certificates against the official statement
data.artifactTitle: Kernel-checked Stable AC certificates against the official statement
data.artifactContent:
This is a partial result toward Stable AC, at every rank. It consists of a verified checker for the challenge's stable move table and a set of theorems about the official relation, all proved in Lean 4 against the unchanged file AC.lean.

The checker. The Discovery Track's move table sac-r8-v1 has 257 moves. We give an executable decoder for all of them and prove that every accepted move is an official step: a stabilization is one StableStep.stabilize at positions (last, last); an accepted destabilization of any relator is one StableStep.destabilize, with the executable renumbering shown to invert Fin.succAbove; ordinary rows reuse the Move.sound theorem of Sneiderman's ordinary checker (theorems stab_sound, destab_sound, step_sound). Replaying an accepted certificate inside the kernel therefore proves

\[
\mathrm{StableReachable}\,\langle 2, R\rangle\,\langle 2, \mathrm{standard}\ 2\rangle
\]

for its starting presentation R (check_sound, checkEncoded_sound). The Discovery verifier ends at the empty presentation and the official conjecture ends at the standard tuple; two official stabilizations bridge the gap inside the proof. A variant accepts certificates from any starting rank (checkEncodedAt_sound).

The official relation. AC.lean states in prose that every move can be undone, that reachability is an equivalence relation, and that the stable conjecture may equivalently end at the empty presentation. We prove these statements as they stand: Step.reverse, StableStep.reverse, Reachable.equivalence, StableReachable.equivalence, stableConjecture_iff_empty, and stableReachable_standard_iff_permuted, so the ordered endpoint adds no restriction. We also prove that presenting the trivial group is invariant along stable paths (StableReachable.presentsTrivialGroup_iff): ordinary moves preserve the normal closure of the relators and stabilization preserves the presented group. Hence the conjecture's hypothesis is a property of the stable class, the conjecture is equivalent to a biconditional (stableConjecture_iff_forall_iff), and an accepted certificate also proves that its starting presentation presents the trivial group.

Substitution. The arguments of Shehper, Medina-Mardones, Fagan, Lewandowski, Gruen, Qiu, Kucharski, Wang and Gukov (arXiv:2408.15332v2, Lemmas 11 and 15) multiply a relator by products of conjugates of the other relators. We prove this mechanism in general: relator i may be right-multiplied by any element of the normal closure of the other relators (Reachable.mulRight_normalClosure), so it may be replaced by any word congruent to it modulo that normal closure, and Lemma 15 follows in its stated form (Reachable.standard_of_congr_generator).

An infinite family. Conjugation trees are presentations whose relators say \(x_i = z_i\, x_{p(i)}^{\pm 1}\, z_i^{-1}\) for arbitrary words \(z_i\) and any parent function with \(i < p(i)\), the last generator being killed. They are AC-trivial at every rank by three official moves per relator (Chain.tree_reachable; chains are \(p(i)=i+1\)). The root relator may be any word congruent to the root generator or its inverse modulo the tree relators (Chain.tree_with_root_reachable), and such presentations are stably trivial and present the trivial group. This is the substitution step of the paper's Theorem 16 and Remark 17 without the knot-diagram hypothesis. The congruence hypothesis cannot be weakened to exponent sum \(\pm 1\) for general trees: the rank-two chain with \(z_1 = x_2 x_1\) is the braid relation, and the repository records a word of exponent sum 1 in the kernel of \(B_3 \to \mathrm{SL}(2,5)\).

Substitution and removal. Lemma 11 of the same paper states that if \(\langle x_1,\dots,x_n, y \mid r_1,\dots,r_n, y^{-1}w\rangle\) presents the trivial group and w is a word in the x, then it is stably AC-equivalent to \(\langle x \mid r_1[w/y],\dots,r_n[w/y]\rangle\). We prove this against the official stable relation with y at any generator position and \(y^{-1}w\) at any relator index (Lemma11.substitution_removal); stable triviality transfers both ways (Lemma11.stableTrivial_iff). The proof substitutes w for y through the normal-closure lemma, transfers triviality to the reduced presentation through the retraction \(y \mapsto w\), replaces \(y^{-1}w\) by y, and removes the pair by one official destabilization. Iterating from a conjugation tree gives the class of Remark 17, and every member is stably trivial (Lemma11.remark17_stableTrivial).

Conjecture 19. We state the paper's Conjecture 19 against the official definitions and prove that it reduces to the case \(w = x_i\): if every generator is congruent to \(x_i^{\pm 1}\) modulo the other relators and \(\langle x \mid r, x_i\rangle\) is AC-trivial, then so is \(\langle x \mid r, w\rangle\) for every w of signed exponent sum \(\pm 1\) (conjecture19_reduction, conjecture19_iff_generator).

What remains open. Neither conjecture is advanced beyond the family and the reduction above. Ordinary AC-triviality of the Remark 17 class (the paper's Conjecture 18) and the case \(w = x_i\) of Conjecture 19 are untouched. The Wirtinger presentations of unknot diagrams, the motivating instances of Theorem 16, are not formalized. The checker enforces no resource limits, which the Discovery verifier does, so acceptance here does not imply acceptance there. No equivalence with the reference verifier is proved; agreement is tested.

Trust base and testing. Lean 4.29.1, Mathlib 5e932f97, AC.lean at commit a0fd6e6 byte-identical, with the hash asserted in CI. Every theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; there is no sorry and no native_decide, and a sorry and a native_decide control both fail the axiom gate. The move table is generated from the official stable_move_spec.json and re-serialized in Lean for a byte-for-byte diff. Against the official Python verifier: 27 of the 33 golden vectors agree on verdict, code, reason and index (the other six concern spec mismatch and resource limits and have no analogue); 200,000 random single moves at ranks 2 to 8 agree; all 848 training paths are accepted by both; 400 generated stable certificates through rank 8, using every move id, are accepted by both; 3,296 one-move mutants agree. Ninety-eight kernel-checked certificates and witnesses accompany the theorems, including the 161-move training path and rank-8 certificates, each in under three seconds. Every test is seeded and recorded in a ledger in the repository.

Reproduction.
```
git clone https://github.com/SAIRcompetition/Andrews-Curtis.git official && git -C official checkout a0fd6e6f52d82c93ccc06ab91d81e8fa3678256e
git clone https://github.com/ibrahimmian36/evocatus.git && cd evocatus && git checkout ace8045d77874d151d47808207a946d266413a4f
cd lean && lake exe cache get && lake build StableCertificate Checks stablecheck && cd ..
ACC_OFFICIAL=$PWD/../official tools/run_all.sh
```

Sources used. Rob Sneiderman's ac-square-divisibility (commit d0ed2c0, Apache-2.0) is a Lake dependency: its unchanged AC module, its ordinary ac-r2-v1 checker (Move, Move.sound, replay, parseTuple) and its stable lemmas (stabilize_at, stabilize_succAbove, stabilize_standard_same) are used directly; this package adds the sac-r8-v1 decoder, the executable stabilization and destabilization with their soundness proofs, and everything above the checker. The official statement, specification and reference verifier are SAIR's. The families and the substitution mechanism formalize arguments from Shehper et al. (arXiv:2408.15332v2), whose text is cited above; Myasnikov, Myasnikov and Shpilrain (arXiv:math/0302080) and Lisitsa (arXiv:2501.18601; J. Comput. Algebra 16 (2025) 100041) are cited for the AK(3) record. Earlier Lean formalization work by Zhang, Zhou, George, Gukov and Anandkumar (NeurIPS 2025 MATH-AI workshop) predates the official statement and is not built on here.

On AK(3). The pool lists AK(3) as sac-00399. Version 1 of arXiv:2408.15332 (2024) stated that AK(3) is stably AC-trivial; the authors withdrew the statement in version 2 (February 2025), tracing it to a misprint in the 13th relator of the Wirtinger presentation in Myasnikov, Myasnikov and Shpilrain (2003), and noting in Appendix F that the presentations involved are not necessarily stably AC-trivial. Lisitsa's automated-deduction paper (January 2025) re-derives the AC-equivalence to AK(3) and inherits the stable step from the same source. Some later citations and the AC-Solver repository still carry the version 1 wording. As far as we can tell, no public replayable stable certificate for AK(3) exists, and the challenge correctly scores it as unsolved. If one appears, the checker here turns it into a kernel theorem.
